newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened against the basket of key foreign currencies on Monday following the sharp decline of the dollar on overseas markets on Friday, dealers said.

"The market was very quiet today. The session opened with slightly more conversions of shekels into dollars and the shekel rose to 3.52 shekels per dollar," said a dealer at the First International Bank of Israel.
"By midday the shekel started declining and it fell to 3.53 shekels per dollar. It seems that the market is stabilising in a range of 3.52 to 3.55 shekels per dollar," he said.
The dealer added that the basket of key foreign currencies rose following the decline of the dollar abroad on Friday.
"The basket is recovering and it is now trading at 0.7 percent below the higher edge of its trading band. I believe that in the near term the central bank will remain out of the market," he said.

The Bank of Israel stopped intervening in the forex market in mid-June, after it slashed interest rates by 1.2 percentage points following a government decision to widen the currency's trading band and lower its crawling slope.
The Bank of Israel will not set a representative rate on Tuesday because of the Jewish fast day of Tisha B'Av.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5300 shekels compared with 3.5330 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7586 against 3.7491 on Friday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.0491 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9862 on Friday, and against the mark at 1.9025 shekels compared with 1.8872 on Friday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5300 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
